This vignette covers Landsat-MODIS data fusion and optional field boundary
priors. Both are experimental and need validation for the intended use.

The examples in this vignette require remote data or a user-supplied field
boundary file and are not evaluated when the package is built. Each main
section starts with its own retrieval, so you can follow either one.

```{r load-ocular}
library(ocular)
```

## Landsat-MODIS data fusion

`add_modis()` uses daily MCD43A4 NBAR data to estimate additional values for
vegetative indices (VI) on dates in the requested period that are not covered
by Landsat. A candidate MCD43A4 date is used only when no Landsat acquisition
falls within three days. The nearest Landsat acquisition provides the anchor,
and each estimate is created on the Landsat grid. A date is skipped when no
MCD43A4 scene lies within one day of its anchor.

The appended scenes are estimates, not satellite observations. They extend
the output series but are excluded from the multi-temporal spectral feature
stack used for field boundary delineation.

### Adding estimated dates

Use an explicit Landsat source and a supported index. The location, dates, and
extent below are illustrative.

```{r add-fused-scenes, eval=FALSE}
rs <- get_rs(
  longitude = 147.227906,
  latitude = -33.0675167,
  start_date = "2016-05-18",
  end_date = "2016-09-21",
  index_name = "NDVI",
  source = "landsat-8",
  x_metres = 1000
)

rs_fused <- add_modis(rs)
field_fused <- boundary_delineation(rs_fused)
fused_series <- as_time_series(field_fused)
head(fused_series)
```

When fusion metadata is present, `is_fused` distinguishes observed Landsat
dates from estimates, and `anchor_days` gives the separation from the anchor.
`anchor_mae` and `anchor_nmae` describe mismatch at that Landsat anchor. They
are construction diagnostics, not held-out prediction errors. If no fusion
metadata was added, or the result is empty, these columns can be absent.

`add_modis()` returns a Sentinel-2 object unchanged. It adds no scenes
when fusion has already been applied, no suitable MCD43A4 scenes are
available, or the selected index lacks the required Landsat and MCD43A4 band
mappings.

### Leave-one-out validation

`validate_data_fusion()` holds out each available Landsat scene in turn,
estimates it from the remaining inputs, and compares the estimate with the
observation. A held-out scene is skipped when it or its anchor has no MCD43A4
scene of its own within one day. The standalone validation call must use the
same output index as the workflow being assessed. Its default is EVI2.

```{r validate-fusion, eval=FALSE}
fusion_validation <- validate_data_fusion(
  147.227906,
  latitude = -33.0675167,
  start_date = "2016-05-18",
  end_date = "2016-09-21",
  index_name = "NDVI",
  source = "landsat-8",
  x_metres = 1000
)

fusion_validation
```

The result has one row per held-out Landsat scene that could be estimated.
`rmse`, `mae`, `bias` (estimate minus observation) and `r` summarise agreement
across paired scene pixels; `n_pixels` gives their count. This call assesses
the retrieved imagery for the query, not the mask in `field_fused`. Its metrics
are not errors in the field-average time series.

If no scene can be estimated, the standalone call returns `NULL`. Metrics are
`NA` with fewer than `min_valid_n` pairs (default four); correlation is also
`NA` for constant values. These results describe the selected query and do not
establish performance elsewhere. See `?validate_data_fusion` for daily
time-series and raster input.

Fusion remains experimental. In particular, product-specific MCD43A4 quality
layers are not currently applied. Retain `is_fused` in downstream data, report
the validation conditions, and avoid presenting estimated dates as observed
Landsat acquisitions.

## Optional field boundary prior

`add_ftw_prior()` reads a user-supplied field boundary GeoParquet and selects
the polygon containing the supplied point. Fields of The World (FTW) is one
field boundary dataset that can be supplied in this form. fiboa is a schema,
not another name for the FTW dataset. The default geometry and date column
names follow that schema and can be overridden for another compatible export.

The selected polygon can supply calibration support. When it also has a usable
source year, it can apply an age-weighted soft prior during the initial area
search. An undated polygon provides calibration support without that
age-weighted prior.

### Attaching a prior

If you want to extract values within an existing polygon directly, use `mask`
in `as_raster()` or `as_time_series()` as shown in
[Getting started](https://github.com/AAGI-AUS/ocular/blob/main/vignettes/ocular-introduction.Rmd). A prior
instead informs delineation and does not impose a fixed output boundary.

Before running this example, you need:

- A compatible field boundary GeoParquet covering the point. The default
  columns are `geometry` and `determination_datetime`; use `geometry_col` and
  `datetime_col` for other names, or `datetime_col = NULL` for undated data.
- The optional `duckdb` and `DBI` R packages, and DuckDB's locally installed
  `spatial` extension. Remote files also need `httpfs`; reading source years
  needs `icu`. ocular does not install extensions automatically. See
  `?add_ftw_prior` for setup requirements.
- The geometry's **source CRS**. `crs = 4326` below assumes the file uses
  EPSG:4326; change it to match your dataset.

Retrieve an object, replace the placeholder path with your file, and attach
the prior before delineation:

```{r attach-field-prior, eval=FALSE}
rs <- get_rs(
  longitude = 147.227906,
  latitude = -33.0675167,
  start_date = "2016-05-18",
  end_date = "2016-09-21",
  index_name = "NDVI",
  source = "landsat-8",
  x_metres = 1000
)

rs_prior <- add_ftw_prior(
  rs,
  source = "/path/to/field-boundaries.parquet",
  crs = 4326
)

field_prior <- boundary_delineation(rs_prior)
terra::plot(as_raster(field_prior))
```

If no field contains the point, ocular reports this and returns the object
unchanged. Delineation can still run, but the default prior diagnostic below
requires a successfully attached prior.

### Interpreting agreement diagnostics

`diagnose_against_ftw()` calculates pixel-level IoU, F1, precision, recall,
and supporting counts between a delineation and a reference polygon.

```{r diagnose-prior, eval=FALSE}
in_sample_diagnostic <- diagnose_against_ftw(field_prior)

# held_out_field_boundary is a user-supplied sf, sfc, or SpatVector object
independent_diagnostic <- diagnose_against_ftw(
  field_prior,
  reference = held_out_field_boundary
)
```

The first call compares the result with the same polygon that supplied the
prior. It is an in-sample diagnostic because that polygon may have influenced
the delineation. Use a separate held-out reference, as in the second call,
when assessing accuracy. The reference needs a defined CRS and must overlap
the feature grid. Record the source file, schema mapping, boundary date, and
whether the reference also supplied the prior.

See `?add_modis`, `?validate_data_fusion`, `?add_ftw_prior`, and
`?diagnose_against_ftw` for the complete interfaces.
